name: hele-shaw-flow
description: Hele-Shaw Flow — the free-boundary flow of a viscous fluid in a Hele-Shaw cell, as a conformal map of the unit disk evolving in time. The exact Graven–Makarov "twisting" showpiece (twist.html): the one-point unbounded quadrature domain QD(α/(w−w₀)) at w₀ = 2 driven by a complex charge α = q + iγ, grown and spun up to a double point or a (3,2)-cusp — everything closed form (=), and drivable by a one-point QD authored in the Quadrature Domains app and handed over as an @cas/interchange link. And the classical interior-droplet Polubarinova–Galin evolver (droplet.html): a bounded droplet grown from a central source by numerical time-stepping of the PG equation (≈) — injection smooths, suction fingers into a (3,2)-cusp (ill-posed) — with the conserved Richardson moments as the honest error bar and a hard ⚠ cusp/suction stop. Split out of 2D Electrostatics (ADR-0036); built on the shared @cas/* packages — @cas/flow (the conformal-transplant kernel + the Net2D line-art drawer), @cas/core (the dftOnCircle spectral primitive), @cas/interchange (the QD → Hele-Shaw hand-off), and @cas/ui (the shared browser shell). Conventions follow the author's paper 'Complex Analysis as Two-Dimensional Electrostatics and Hydrodynamics' at the app edge.
author: Andrew Graven <andrew@graven.com>
